newsitem.title: USA: California quake agency says will meet requirement.
newsitem.headline: California quake agency says will meet requirement.

text.p: The California Earthquake Authority (CEA) will meet its residential insurance market requirement, allowing it to become operational on December 1, its chief executive said on Monday.

The authority had so far secured the backing of 69.7 percent of California's residential insurance market, just short of the 70 percent that was required, said Greg Butler the authority's interim chief executive.

To lift the CEA above the 70 percent mark, the authority's governing board on Tuesday was expected to incorporate the state's independent Fair Access to Insurance Requirement (FAIR) plan within the CEA. The FAIR plan provides homeowners insurance to those that cannot find insurance elsewhere.
By incorporating the FAIR plan, the CEA would assume its market share, equal to roughly one percent of the earthquake insurance market, Butler said.
"We will have the 70 percent if the board approves the FAIR plan," Butler said "I don't expect a problem."

Insurance companies representing at least 70 percent of the California residential insurance market had to agree to participate in the earthquake authority by the Nov. 25 deadline in order for the authority to become operational.
The CEA had set earlier deadlines but decided to give insurance companies more time.
Assuming the CEA incorporates FAIR, the earthquake authority should become operational as planned on December 1 to begin selling insurance policies, Butler said.

With the participation of 70 percent of the market, the insurance industry would contribute an initial $700 million to fund the earthquake authority. The industry would be obligated to make additional capital commitments to pay claims if an earthquake strikes.
